subject: Capacity reconciliation & burst plan ahead of NovaHealth renewal
messages:
From: Alex Moreno <alex@novahealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: priya.shah@novahealth.com
Date: Sat, 1 May 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity — utilization vs committed ahead of renewal

Hi team,

We’re starting prep for our renewal later this month and wanted to align on a couple of items around dedicated GPU sizing. Our platform saw a couple of sustained spikes in April that pushed our billed throughput well above the committed fleet for several hours (logs attached to this message). We want to understand:

- How your utilization numbers map to the committed GPUs vs burst pools (we see a gap in our internal telemetry).
- Whether adding capacity now vs adjusting the commit at renewal makes sense from a cost/availability standpoint.
- Any recommended burst schedule/policy you would suggest given our traffic pattern (weekday-heavy daytime spikes).

Can someone run a reconciliation against our current tranche and share a proposed path (short-term burst vs commit change) so we can include it in the renewal PO? We prefer minimal downtime and to avoid a full overcommit.

Thanks,
Alex
Head of ML Ops
NovaHealth

Attachments: nova-telemetry-apr-2027.log (log stub)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Alex Moreno <alex@novahealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — utilization vs committed ahead of renewal

Hi Alex — thanks for the heads up and the telemetry. I pulled the last 90 days of serving metrics and ran a utilization reconciliation; attaching the CSV with minute-level summaries (nova-usage-report-may2027.csv). Quick summary up front: 

- Committed capacity today: 120 A100-equivalent GPUs (tranche-3).
- Observed steady-state average utilization: ~58% aggregated across the fleet over the 30-day window.
- 95th percentile sustained window (1h bins): 82% utilization.
- Peak short bursts (<=15m): 98% on three separate days (weekday business hours).
- Estimated unmet demand (requests that experienced queuing or fell back to smaller models): ~6.2% of tokens during peaks.

Recommendation (short + medium term):
1) Short-term burst pool: add a configurable 36-GPU burst pool for predictable weekday spikes (Mon–Fri 08:00–18:00 local). This can be a shared burst group we keep for NovaHealth and auto-scale down outside windows.
2) Renewal commit: move to a 150-GPU committed baseline ( +30 GPUs ) with a 90-day review. That reduces sustained utilization to ~47% and removes the majority of peak queuing events.
3) Canary rollout: stage the 36 GPUs in two 18-GPU phases across two weeks to validate throughput, KV-cache warmup, and latency SLAs — we’ll instrument trace-level latency for top-10 routes during each phase.

Cost/impact: I ran a quick unit-cost estimate: short-term burst (36 GPUs) billed as burst at on-demand rates; shifting +30 GPUs into commit will increase your monthly committed spend but lowers per-token marginal cost and avoids burst premium long-term. Marissa, I’ll let you include specific pricing/discount language.

I’ve attached a proposed burst schedule PDF and the CSV export. If that approach looks good, we can turn this into a mutual action plan and DocuSign amendment for the renewal.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments: nova-usage-report-may2027.csv; proposed-burst-schedule.pdf

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Alex Moreno <alex@novahealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — utilization vs committed ahead of renewal

Alex — appreciate the details. Pricing notes to make contracting simple: 

- Option A (Recommended): Commit +30 GPUs (150 total) for a 12-month term. We can offer a 12% commit discount on those additional GPUs and waive the one-time provisioning fee.
- Option B: Keep existing commit (120 GPUs) and add 36-GPU burst pool billed at on-demand with a monthly cap (we can set an upper bound so spend is predictable).

I’ve started a draft amendment (nova-renewal-mop-v1.docx) with language for Option A. If finance is comfortable we can attach the DocuSign link and route for signatures. For Option B we’ll need clear burst caps and an SLA addendum for how fallback to smaller models is handled during sustained spikes.

Next steps: please confirm which path you prefer by EOD Friday and we’ll prepare the amendment. Suggested meeting to finalize: Thursday 10am PT (30m).

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: nova-renewal-mop-v1.docx

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — utilization vs committed ahead of renewal

Looping in from the infra side — technical signoff and notes: 

- Feasibility: +30 committed GPUs and a 36-GPU burst pool are both straightforward. We recommend using an isolated burst pool with automated KV cache seeding to reduce cold-start latency on scale-ups.
- Canary plan: propose phase 1 (18 GPUs) for 48 hours during a simulated weekday peak; phase 2 (another 18 GPUs) after we validate cache warmup and request routing.
- Observability hooks: we’ll add a temporary per-route tracing tag and a cost/latency dashboard tile for NovaHealth so product + ops can watch the rollout in near real time.

Happy to run the canary with you — we’ll coordinate blackout windows for any infra ops that may impact traffic.

Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Moreno <alex@novahealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: priya.shah@novahealth.com
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — utilization vs committed ahead of renewal

Thanks everyone — this plan looks reasonable. We’ll take Option A (commit +30 GPUs for 12 months) with the proposed 12% discount and the two-step canary for the 36-GPU burst pool.

Action items we need from Redwood:
- Final amendment in DocuSign (Marissa)
- CSV usage reconciliation and a one-page summary for our procurement team (Karthik)
- Kickoff call to schedule canary windows and share runbooks (suggest Thursday 10am PT)

We’ll prepare a PO once DocuSign is signed.

Alex
Head of ML Ops, NovaHealth
